content.text: No non-compete, exclusivity, or field-of-use restriction on Customer's businesses or products exists anywhere in the Agreement. I confirmed the only candidate provisions are licence-scope terms on M&I's own deliverables.

input.quote: Customer agrees that, except as otherwise permitted in this Agreement or in writing by M&I, Customer will use the Services only for its own internal business purposes to service its banking customers and clients and will not sell or otherwise provide, directly or indirectly, any of the Services or any portion thereof to any third party
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no non-compete, exclusivity, or field-of-use restriction on Customer, so the preferred position is met and no redline is warranted. I checked every plausible location: Article 3 (Appointment) contains no exclusivity or requirements commitment; Article 2 (Term) is renewal-only; and the only "compet-" hit is "court or arbitrator of competent jurisdiction" in Section 22.10. Section 21.11 (Future Acquisitions) does not restrict Customer's businesses — it expressly contemplates new branches, new operations, acquisitions of Control of additional financial institutions and a Change in Control, and only addresses fees, conversion scheduling and the scope of M&I's continuing service obligation. The two use-limitation provisions (Section 21.7(B), quoted, and Section 23.5 on escrowed source code) are scope-of-licence/no-resale terms governing M&I's own Services and source code; they do not limit the businesses Customer may operate or the products Customer may buy or build, so they are outside this rule. Restrictions binding M&I are not flagged.
